chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a traveler who entered his home before the sun's declination (midday) and had already eaten. He said: It is not appropriate for him to eat anything that day, nor to have sexual intercourse during the month of Ramadan, if he has a family.

key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Declination of the sun; midday, the time when the sun reaches its zenith and the Dhuhr prayer time begins.
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramadan, during which fasting is obligatory.
key_terms.يُوَاقِعَ: To have sexual intercourse; the act that breaks the fast in Ramadan.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who returns home during Ramadan before midday and has already eaten?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Istibsar, the Imam establishes that a traveler who returns before midday (zawal) and has already eaten must abstain from further eating and sexual intercourse for the remainder of the day, effectively treating their status as a fasting person. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the obligation to fast applies immediately upon the traveler's return, even if they have not yet performed the formal intention (niyyah) or eaten their pre-dawn meal (suhoor) in the new location, emphasizing the continuity of the fast once the exemption of travel ends.
